title.narrative: Enhancing Collection of Revenue and Expenditure Management Project

description.narrative: The ENCORE remains a well-performing project supporting difficult governance reforms that are critical to the national development priorities of DRC. The proposed Additional Financing will scale up activities to buttress expenditure management reforms implemented under ENCORE and include deepened support for independent oversight arrangements at central level. The AF will also expand support for improved resource management to three additional provinces (Kongo Central, Equateur, and Maniema).
The project development objective is to increase mining revenue transparency and improve expenditure management at the central level and in the project provinces

title.narrative: Percentage increase in Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) collected by project provinces

comment.narrative: This indicator tracks progress recorded in IGR in the four project provinces. The baseline is the average annual percentage change in nominal IGR growth for the 10 selected CPF focus provinces in 2017, 2018 and 2019 (before COVID19). The targets are expected annual percentage increases in nominal IGR growth for the four project provinces. The final target is to have provinces increase their nominal IGR by one third compared to total revenue collected in 2021. In 2022, the average increase (from 2021) in IGR was 7.6%. In 2023, the average increase was -7.53%. By March the data for two provinces was reported with Kasai Central -16.6% and Kasai Oriental 65.66% year to year increase in the average.The project has financed taxpayer census in the respective provinces in 2023 and 2024, and trainnings on tax collection procedures for 321 tax collectors, the purchase of 400 motorcicles to be used by tax collectors, the drafting of a procures manual for the colletion of local taxes and fees.

comment.narrative: The two decrees pertaining to the indicator have been adopted. The decree for the allocation of mining royalties to provinces (25%) and ETDs (15%) was published in the Official Gazette in May 2022.â€¯Between 2022 and 2023 a string of decrees were signed to create a total of 46 entities that will oversee the implementation of the 0.3% sharing arrangement in Haut-Katanga, Lualaba, Kasai-Oriental, North Kivu, and Ituri.â€¯The EITI -DRC Secretariat has followed the implementation of the decrees and developed a mechanism to monitor the use of the 0.3% sharing arrangement. By the end of December 2023, ten of the entities created for the management of the 0.3% presented their management reports which include details on the community development program funded. Additionally, the EITI-DRC Secretariat is actively monitoring the use of the funds and is set to report on this in their 2022 report. The upcoming audits by the Court of Auditors will further scrutinize the management of the funds.

comment.narrative: This indicator is composed of 3 EITI requirements that the project is supporting through its activities. Since the May 2024 mission, satisfactory progress has been made in the production of the 2022 EITI-DRC Report scoping report, with the publication of the results of the use of the 0.3% revenue sharing agreement of mining companies, which would thus advance compliance with EITI requirements. title.narrative: Number of Accounting Department Units (DGTCP) operational in provinces

comment.narrative: This indicator will track the deployment of Accounting Provincial Units. No Accounting Provincial Units have been established yet. The establishment of acounting units and assignment of accountants in the Provinces will follow the effective deconcentration of the first eight Ministries. The mapping of accounting posts was carried out in six provinces (KasaÃ¯ Oriental, KasaÃ¯, KasaÃ¯ Central, Lomami, Kinshasa, Kongo Central). A new roadmap was drawn up in August 2024, at the request of the new Minister of Finance, for the operationalisation of the DGTCP, whose actions extend until 2028. This roadmap provides for the revision of the institutional and procedural framework governing the keeping of public accounting, including Decree No. 22/12B on the creation, missions and functioning of the DGTCP and Decree No. 13/050 on the general regulation on public accounting (adopted by the Council of Ministers on October 4, 2024)

title.narrative: Number of Accounting Department Units (DGTCP) operational in provinces

comment.narrative: This indicator will track the deployment of Accounting Provincial Units. No Accounting Provincial Units have been established yet. The roadmap for the establishment of the DGTCP adopted in August 2024 provides prerequisites for the deployment of accounting positions in the provinces. Among these, a mapping of accounting posts in six provinces of the first phase (Kasai Oriental, Kasai, Kasai Central, Lomami, Kinshasa, Kongo Central) was carried out. Additional prerequisites to implementation or provincial DGTCPs are: (i) the designation of the TPP (Tresorerie Payerie Provinciale), TPU (Tresorerie Payerie Urbaine), TPT (Tresorerie Payerie Territoriale) and their secondary accountants as well as the administrative staff for the accounting positions; (ii) the swearing-in and installation of TPPs, TPUs and TPTs and secondary accountants, as well as training on general bookkeeping tools in decentralised mode; (iii) the opening of the operating account of the TPP, TPU and TPT.

title.narrative: Selected strategic SOEs publishing annual financial audit reports

comment.narrative: This indicator tracks increased transparency of the following nine major SOEs: SNEL, REGIDESO, RVA, SNCC, SCTP, SCPT, Gecamines, Miba, and Sokimo. Gecamines Financial Reports were published in 2021 (baseline).â€¯ In collaboration with the IMF, the consolidated financial situation of 20 SOEs was gathered and included as annex to the 2024 budget law sent to parliament. The 2022 audited financial statements for Gecamines, SNEL and REGIDESO were published in March 2024 by the Superior Council Portofolio (https://csp.cd/etats-financieres-entreprises/). To strengthen the oversight and coordination of SOEs, the following actions have been initiated with project support : (i) the development of a portal at the enterprise level on the information to be collected and exchanged, with the possibility of online interaction with the CSP; (ii) the development of a procedures manual for the control and audit of SOES, (iii) the acquisition of computer equipment and consumables for the CSP.

title.narrative: Number of Line Ministries trusted with budget commitment authority (PBC #1)

baseline.value: Budget commitment authority is concentrated at the Ministry of Finance level. No Line Ministry is granted with the budget commitment authority.

target.value: PBC#1.5: Budget commitment authority transferred to eight (8) Line Ministries.

comment.narrative: The indicator tracks the decentralization of budget authority to eight ministries. The IT prerequisites are ready to make effective the decentralization of budget authority in four line ministries : Public Health, Education, Rural Development, and Public Works. The GesdApenses system has been set up and tested in the pilot ministries, and IT equipment has been deployed there. Tasks expected for the operationalization of the decentralization of budget authority in these four pilot ministries in December 2024 have not yet been carried out, these are: (i) the assignment of accountants; (ii) opening designated accounts after a finance ministry and central bank agreement on the single treasury account, (iii) implementing the new accounting systems. The New Minister of Finance, in office since June 2024, has requested new roadmaps for the commissioning of the DGTCP and for the operationalization of the decentralization of budget authority.

actual.value: Budget commitment authority is not transferred to any line ministry

title.narrative: Number of Line Ministries trusted with budget commitment authority (PBC #1)

target.value: PBC#1.5: Budget commitment authority transferred to eight (8) Line Ministries.

comment.narrative: A feasibility study for the extension of the expenditure chain in five other pilot ministries (National defence, Higher and University Education, Agriculture, Fisheries and Livestock, and Finance) with a view to the deconcentration of the budgetary commitment authority has been carried out, thus increasing the number of pilot ministries to nine. Also, an interministerial decreerevising the expenditure chain manual was signed on December 20, 2024. Progress has been made on accounting prerequisites, with the signing of the central government's single account-keeping agreement with the Central Bank on December 31, 2024, and the signing of the decree establishing transitional provisions for the operationalization of the DGTCP on March 7, 2025. On April 30, 2025, 7 decrees were signed, 6 of which relate to the creation of the six accounting positions for the nine pilot ministries and 1 determining the regulations relating to the competitive recruitment of public accountants.

The validation phase has been completed in 13 provinces and is underway in 4 others. The directories of certified civil servants for the project provinces (Kasai, Kasai Central, Kasai Oriental and Lomami) were published in January 2025. Thus, the PBC#21-2.4 has been achieved with the cleaning up of the civil servants' database at the central Government and the city of Kinshasa (PBC#2.1) and the three Kasai provinces (PBC#2.2) in 2024, as well as the provinces of Lomami, Kongo Central and Kwilu (PBC#2.3), and the provinces of Equateur, Haut Katanga and Lualaba (PBC#2.4) between January and April 2025. comment.narrative: This indicator tracks the implementation of the poverty survey activities from collection of data until the production and dissemination of survey results and reports.â€¯ Three specialists (RA, CAPI, and survey experts) were hired to support the preparation of statistical activities, which include a survey on non-standard units (NSU) and a survey of household living conditions. title.narrative: Consolidated, relevant, and comprehensive budget reports and financial statements in project provinces are produced and available

baseline.value: Quarterly budget reports are prepared and published in none of the project provinces. No Annual Financial reports meeting accounting standards is currently prepared

target.value: Quarterly budget reports are prepared and regularly published on all four project provinces websites and financial reports meeting new accounting standards are produced by existing DGTCP provincial units, then submitted to CoA

comment.narrative: In mid-December 2024, three of the four provinces in the project's intervention area disseminated the 2024 mid-term budget report. The Provinces of Kasai Oriental and Lomami distributed copies to civil society, which participated in the budget conferences, and to public services, while the Province of Kasai Central publicly displayed its report in the offices of the five communes of Kananga. In 2025, actions to strengthen budget management and rationalize expenditure management in the provinces included training of experts from the provincial budget divisions of the provinces supported, coaching of key services of the provincial ministries of the budget, training of users on the model budget edict and the computer tool for preparing the budget; and work on drawing up the budget edict for the year 2025 using the IT tool developed.

actual.value: In mid-December 2024, three of the four provinces in the project's intervention area disseminated the 2024 mid-term budget report.

title.narrative: Share of line ministries using e-procurement system (PBC#3)

baseline.value: SIGMAP, a system already developed by the government, is ready to be rolled out.

target.value: PBC#3.5: The E-procurement system is operational in one (1) additional Line Ministry.

comment.narrative: The final regulatory prerequisite was achieved with the signing of the ministerial decree on the implementation of the digital platform for the management of public procurement in the DRC by the Minister of the Budget on March 13, 2025 and the circular on the SIGMAP user manual making the use of the e-procurement system in the DRC mandatory. Two rooms dedicated to SIGMAP have been set up at the Ministry of Budget. They require appropriate equipment to ensure the confidentiality of SIGMAP users who will come from other units. Retraining of trained staff in the 20 pilot entities in the use of SIGMAP is required before the rolling out step scheduled for July 1, 2025. The contract to recruit the firm for the development, configuration, and deployment of e-GPs was negotiated and the minutes of negotiations signed. The contract will be sent to the Bank for no objection in June.

actual.value: The SIGMAP is not currently operational. The e-GP system has not been aquired.

title.narrative: Number of Accounting Department Units (DGTCP) operational in central ministries

baseline.value: The national Accounting Department (DGTCP) is not yet formally established

target.value: Accounting Department (DGTCP) Unit is established in one additional line ministry

comment.narrative: Eight decrees have been issued to accelerate the operationalization of the DGTCP during the first four months of 2025, the first setting out the transitional provisions relating to the operationalization of the DGTCP (March 7, 2025), six other creating six accounting positions for nine ministries and repealing the eight decrees that created four accounting positions in 2023 and four additional positions in 2024 (April 30, 2025). The specificity of these six decrees of 2025 lies in the composition and internal organization of the accounting posts (from four public accountants to a dozen ones with several offices, including for the production of financial statements and a secretariat). The eighth decree determines the rules for the organization of the competitive recruitment of public accountants and administrative agents for the six accounting positions (April 30, 2025).

actual.value: No accounting units are operational in the central ministries.

title.narrative: Number of Accounting Department Units (DGTCP) operational in central ministries

baseline.value: The national Accounting Department (DGTCP) is not yet formally established

target.value: Accounting Department (DGTCP) Unit is established in one additional line ministry

comment.narrative: The DGTCP was made operational with the establishment of the national network of accountants, in March 2023, and the appointment of key staff: Director General, two Deputy Directors General (of which one is female), and seven director-level positions (of which two are female). The network of accountants interministerial edict of March 2023 also established the first accounting units in the Ministries of Public Health; Primary Education; Rural Development; and Public Works. Each unit would need one principal public accountant, one secondary public accountant, two administrative staff. To make the accounting units operational there remains (i) the appointment of the staff; (ii) the roll-out and adoption of the accounting system; the (iii) signing of the Central Bank-Ministry of Finance convention for the single treasury account; and (iv) subsequent opening of designated accounts for the respective accountants. All of these prerequisites are expected to be met by the end of the 2024.

actual.value: No accounting units are operational in the central ministries.
